title: App Gets Berliners to Water City Trees
paragraphs: Hot and dry summers are making life difficult for trees in many cities. In Berlin, Germany, a free app is encouraging residents to help by watering the trees in their neighborhoods.
The project is called "Gieß den Kiez," which means "Water the Neighborhood." It was started in 2020 by CityLAB Berlin, part of a technology foundation called Technologiestiftung Berlin.

The app shows an interactive map of hundreds of thousands of street and park trees in Berlin. For each tree, users can see information such as its species, its age and how much water it needs. The app also uses daily data from Germany's weather service to show how much rain has fallen on each tree over the past 30 days. In addition, it shows the locations of public water pumps.

Residents can type in their address to find trees near their home that need water. After they water a tree, they can record it in the app, so that other people can see which trees still need attention. Users can also "adopt" trees that they water regularly.

Why is this needed? Because of climate change, Berlin's trees are under stress from hot, dry summers. More trees have been cut down in recent years, and trees are not living as long. Before the app, people who wanted to help often did not know which trees needed water most.

The project has become very popular with local residents. According to one report, around 12,000 people now water trees, working together with the city's maintenance teams. Anna Mehrländer, who leads the project, said she was surprised by how much people care about trees.
Because the app's code is open source, other German cities, such as Leipzig and Magdeburg, have started similar projects.
